confirmed.title: _clear_context unlocks the context layers before the parent 'Gordium', so with 'Gordium' locked the parent's IsVisible call locks them again and every delete fails silently
confirmed.detail: The unlock loop runs over `indexes + parents`, so the context layers are unlocked first and the parent 'Gordium' comes last. The author's own Rhino 8 finding (round 4, built into the round-5 test's _Layer.IsVisible setter) is that setting a parent's IsVisible passes the parent's lock down to every sublayer. So when the architect has locked the 'Gordium' layer, `doc.Layers[k].IsVisible = True` on 'Gordium' locks all five context layers again. Only after that does it unlock 'Gordium' itself. The delete loop then runs on locked layers. `doc.Objects.Delete(o, True)` (which does not ignore modes) returns False, the code never checks it, and `ModifyAttributes` fails the same way. The old outlines stay, and draw_context draws the new neighbourhood next to them: the outlines are doubled, or an old address's neighbourhood is left behind. This is exactly the 'locked or hidden parent ("Gordium")' case the round-4 parent handling was added for. I ran the real _clear_context against the test's own _Layer model with 'Gordium'.IsLocked=True. At FindByLayer time the locks were {'Gordium::Context': True, '...::Parcels': True, '...::Streets': True, '...::Buildings': True, '...::Notes': True}.
confirmed.evidence:
for i in indexes + [k for k, _, _ in parents]:

The test model (test_context_box.py _Layer.IsVisible setter): `for sub in self.table: if sub.FullPath.startswith(self.FullPath + "::"): sub.IsLocked = self.IsLocked`
confirmed.pin: In test_context_box.py, a variant of test_showing_or_hiding_the_neighbourhood_keeps_its_layers_locked_in_rhino_8: set doc.Layers[0] ('Gordium').IsLocked = True and give doc.Objects.FindByLayer a stub that records layer.IsLocked. Run ns['_clear_context'](doc) and assert every recorded lock is False when the objects are read (it fails today: all True).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Unlock and show from the outermost layer inward: the parents first (top ancestor first), then the context layers. After the delete, restore the parents first and then the context layers. Better still, set IsVisible and IsLocked on each layer and then re-assert IsLocked=False on every layer in the touched subtree just before the delete loop. Also check Delete's and ModifyAttributes' return values, so a failed delete makes Gordium say the neighbourhood could not be cleared instead of drawing over it.
skeptics: I read apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:2469-2520 (_clear_context). This code is new in this PR; it is not on origin/start-box-lookup. The parent handling (lines ~2478-2487, the parents list) and the loop `for i in indexes + [k for k, _, _ in parents]:` show the context layers first and the parent 'Gordium' last. The Rhino 8 behaviour that the author records in packages/design_checker/tests/test_context_box.py:968-990 (_Layer.IsVisible setter: every sublayer gets the layer's current IsLocked) means that setting 'Gordium'.IsVisible = True while 'Gordium' is still locked locks all the context sublayers again. 'Gordium'.IsLocked = False only runs after that. The delete loop then calls doc.Objects.Delete(o, True) and ModifyAttributes on locked layers and never checks what they return. I reproduced this by running the real _clear_context source against the test's own _context_doc/_Layer model, with 'Gordium'.IsLocked=True and FindByLayer patched to record each layer's lock. When FindByLayer ran, every context layer was locked: Context, Parcels, Streets, Buildings and Notes were all True. The existing test (test_showing_or_hiding_the_neighbourhood_keeps_its_layers_locked_in_rhino_8) only covers an unlocked 'Gordium', so it does not catch this. Nothing earlier in the function prevents it, because the parents are deliberately handled after the context layers. The simple fix is to show and unlock the parents first, outermost first. Caveat: real Rhino might restore the children's locks through persistent locking when the parent is unlocked. Even so, Parcels, Streets and Notes would come back locked, so the finding holds both under the author's own Rhino 8 model and plausibly in real Rhino.

I couldn't refute it. I read apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py, in _clear_context, at about lines 2470-2516. The parent chain is collected into `parents`. The unlock loop then runs `for i in indexes + [k for k, _, _ in parents]`, which puts IsVisible=True before IsLocked=False on each layer, so the parent "Gordium" is handled last. The delete loop that follows (`doc.Objects.Delete(o, True)` and `ModifyAttributes(o, attrs, True)`) never checks the return value. The test's own Rhino 8 layer model is in packages/design_checker/tests/test_context_box.py:968-990. Its docstring says setting a layer's IsVisible, even to the value it already has, gives every sublayer that layer's lock. So setting 'Gordium'.IsVisible while 'Gordium' is still locked locks every Gordium::Context layer again. I ran the real _clear_context, using the same exec harness as test_showing_or_hiding_the_neighbourhood_keeps_its_layers_locked_in_rhino_8, with doc.Layers[0] ('Gordium') set to IsLocked=True and FindByLayer instrumented. At delete time all five layers were locked: Context, Parcels, Streets, Buildings and Notes all read True. Nothing upstream stops this. The round-4 parent handling exists for exactly the locked 'Gordium' case, its test (line 607) only checks where the text sits in the function, and the round-4 behaviour test (line 1013) only runs with 'Gordium' unlocked. Delete without ignoring modes fails on locked layers; the docstring of _clear_context says so itself. So the old outlines would stay. One caveat: the Rhino lock-passing behaviour comes from the author's documented Rhino 8 finding, which the test model encodes. I didn't run it in Rhino myself. The fix is to unlock the parents first, outermost first, before the context layers.

confirmed.title: Each _clear_context unlocks the architect's other Gordium sublayers (Grade, Grade::Finished, Massing): restoring the parent's IsVisible passes its lock down and _lock_context only puts the context layers back
confirmed.detail: The round-4 fix re-locks only the layers under Gordium::Context (`_lock_context` goes through `_context_layer_indexes`). But the parent whose IsVisible _clear_context sets is 'Gordium', and that layer also holds Gordium::Grade (spot grades), Gordium::Grade::Finished and Gordium::Massing. Under the same Rhino 8 behaviour, `IsVisible = True` and then `IsVisible = was_visible` on 'Gordium' give those sublayers Gordium's lock at that moment. At the restore that lock is False, because the earlier loop set it with `IsLocked = False`, and `IsLocked = was_locked` is only applied afterwards. So if the architect locked Gordium::Grade to protect their spot grades, the lock is lost after every GordiumStart Draw, Edit site lookup or neighbourhood redraw (sync_context and draw_context both call _clear_context). I confirmed this with the real function on the test's _Layer model: a Gordium::Grade layer locked before _clear_context comes out IsLocked=False, whether 'Gordium' was locked or not. This is the same pattern as prior finding 1, fixed only for the context layers.
confirmed.evidence:
for k, was_visible, was_locked in parents:
        doc.Layers[k].IsVisible = was_visible
        doc.Layers[k].IsLocked = was_locked
    _lock_context(doc, True)               # a parent's IsVisible just gave its sublayers its lock (Rhino 8): again

_lock_context covers only `_context_layer_indexes(doc)` (`logic.on_layer(layer.FullPath, logic.CONTEXT)`); GRADE_LAYER = "Gordium::Grade", FINISHED_LAYER = "Gordium::Grade::Finished", MASSING = "Gordium::Massing".
confirmed.pin: In test_context_box.py, extend _context_doc with a 'Gordium::Grade' layer (parent 'Gordium') set IsLocked=True before ns['_clear_context'](doc). Assert it is still locked afterwards (it fails today).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Before changing any parent, record (IsVisible, IsLocked) for every layer under each touched parent, not just the context layers. Once the parents are restored, put each recorded layer's IsLocked back (and its visibility, if Rhino changes that too), then apply _lock_context for the context layers. Better: don't change the parent's IsVisible unless it is actually hidden, and use doc.Objects.Delete(o, True) only after an explicit, scoped unlock.

I could not refute this finding. It holds.

What I read in apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py:
- `_clear_context` (about lines 2470-2516) climbs from each context layer up to its ancestors and collects 'Gordium' in `parents`.
- For each layer in `indexes + parents`, it first sets `IsVisible = True` and then `IsLocked = False`.
- At the restore, it sets `IsVisible = was_visible` first and `IsLocked = was_locked` second.
- After that, the only re-lock is `_lock_context` (line 2423). That function goes only through `_context_layer_indexes` (line 2418), which keeps just the layers for which `logic.on_layer(FullPath, CONTEXT)` is true. Gordium::Grade and Gordium::Massing are not among them.

How I checked it:
- The PR's own test model does propagate the lock. `_Layer` in packages/design_checker/tests/test_context_box.py:968-990 says that setting a layer's IsVisible gives every sublayer that layer's current lock.
- I ran the real `_clear_context` source against that model, with a Gordium::Grade layer added and locked. Grade came out `IsLocked=False` both when 'Gordium' was locked and when it was not. 'Gordium' itself was put back correctly.
- The cause is the order. At the restore, Gordium's IsVisible is set while it is still unlocked, and its real lock only comes back on the next line. So Gordium's unlocked state is what reaches its sublayers.

Upstream guarantee: none. There is no other step that restores the lock on non-context sublayers.

New code or pre-existing: new in this PR. `_clear_context` does not exist on origin/start-box-lookup (grep finds 0 matches there).

Caveat: the finding rests on the Rhino 8 rule that setting a parent's visibility hands its lock down to its sublayers. I took that rule from the PR's own code comment and test model, not from testing in real Rhino.

I could not refute this. I read apps/rhino_plugin/gordium_rhino.py lines 2470-2518 (_clear_context) and 2418-2426 (_context_layer_indexes and _lock_context). The parents loop (2481-2489) collects the ancestors of the context layers, which means 'Gordium' itself. Lines 2491-2493 set IsVisible=True and then IsLocked=False on 'Gordium'. Lines 2509-2511 restore it in the order IsVisible=was_visible first, then IsLocked=was_locked. So at the moment its IsVisible is set, 'Gordium' is unlocked. _lock_context (2512) re-locks only layers that match on_layer(FullPath, 'Gordium::Context') (rhino_logic.py:25), so Gordium::Grade (line 99), Gordium::Grade::Finished (line 100) and Gordium::Massing (rhino_logic.py:12) are never put back.

The Rhino 8 behaviour the finding relies on is not a guess by the reviewer. The project documents it itself: docs/evidence/pr-23/README.md:59-63 says setting a parent's IsVisible gives each sublayer the parent's lock, and the comment at gordium_rhino.py:2512 says the same. The test's _Layer model (test_context_box.py:968-990) encodes it.

I ran the real _clear_context against that model with a Gordium::Grade layer added and locked. It came out IsLocked=False whether 'Gordium' was locked or not, which matches the reviewer's claim. The function is reachable from lines 2598 and 2659 (the sync and draw paths). The code is new in this PR: the diff adds the parents loop and the _lock_context call, so this is not a pre-existing issue. The existing test (test_context_box.py:1013) only checks the context layers, which is why it misses this.

priorStatus.title: Every context layer comes out unlocked after GordiumStart: _context_visible sets the parent Gordium::Context's IsVisible, which in Rhino 8 gives sublayers the parent's (unlocked) lock
priorStatus.reasoning: _context_visible now calls _lock_context(doc, True) after the visibility loop, which fixes the reported case: Gordium::Context's descendants are exactly the layers _lock_context covers. _clear_context also re-locks the context layers after the parent restore. But the same mechanism in _clear_context (setting IsVisible on the parent 'Gordium') also clobbers the locks of Gordium's other sublayers (Grade, Grade::Finished, Massing), which nothing puts back. And the unlock loop's order (context layers before the parents) re-locks the context layers when 'Gordium' is locked, so the delete fails. Both were confirmed by running the real functions on the round-5 test's own _Layer model. The new pin covers only an unlocked 'Gordium' with no other sublayers.

priorStatus.title: FINGERPRINT_ATTRIBUTES omits Rhino 8's LinetypePatternScale though its comment claims every attribute an architect can change in Rhino 7 and 8
priorStatus.reasoning: LinetypePatternScale is in FINGERPRINT_ATTRIBUTES. _attrs_print's broad except leaves it out where Rhino lacks it. attribute_text renders a float stably (repr(round(v, 9))). The test exec's the real _attrs_print and asserts that 1.0 -> 2.0 counts as an edit. A cross-version mismatch is not possible: the plugin is `#! python3` and runs in Rhino 8 only. The comment still says 'Rhino 7 or 8', which is harmless.
